definitions.explanation: Understanding each other without words; communicating through unspoken feelings. A Buddhist-origin four-character idiom.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夫婦|ふうふ}→夫婦：03592_fuufu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{以心伝心|いしんでんしん}⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
examples.english: That couple really understands each other without speaking.

examples.japanese: {以心伝心|いしんでんしん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{気持|きも}ち→気持ち：01385_kimochi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦わかった→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧。
examples.english: I understood his feelings without him saying anything.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長年|ながねん}→長年：09684_naganen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{以心伝心|いしんでんしん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{通|つう}じ→通じる：02289_tsuujiru⟧⟦{合|あ}える→合う：10466_au⟧。
examples.english: With long-time friends, we can communicate without words.

notes:
{以心伝心|いしんでんしん} is a four-character idiom (⟦{四字熟語|よじじゅくご}→四字熟語：15663_yojijukugo⟧) meaning tacit understanding or heart-to-heart communication.

ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{以|い}→以：noentry⟧ (by means of) + ⟦{心|しん}→心：01321_kokoro⟧ (mind) + ⟦{伝|でん}→伝：noentry⟧ (transmit) + ⟦{心|しん}→心：01321_kokoro⟧ (mind) = 'transmitting mind with mind'
Originally a Zen Buddhist term for the transmission of enlightenment from master to disciple beyond words and scriptures.

MODERN USAGE:
Describes intuitive understanding between people who know each other well - couples, close friends, long-time colleagues.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {以心伝心|いしんでんしん}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{通|つう}じ→通じる：02289_tsuujiru⟧⟦{合|あ}う→合う：10466_au⟧: to communicate without words
- {以心伝心|いしんでんしん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧: a relationship with tacit understanding
